author: Rahul kp
title: ABC vs
simple_words: Traditional spreads overhead by volume. ABC charges it by the activities each product actually uses.

definitions.meaning: Overheads are collected by department and absorbed on a volume base such as labour hours or machine hours.
Overheads are collected in activity cost pools and charged to products by cost drivers, the cause of each activity's cost.

key_points: Traditional costing assumes ==volume== causes overhead; ABC assumes ==activities== cause it.
ABC links cost to the real driver: set-ups, orders, inspections, machine runs.
Traditional costing tends to over-cost high-volume simple products and under-cost low-volume complex ones.
!!ABC does not change total overhead!!; it only changes how it is shared among products.

insight.text: Both methods recover the same total overhead; they differ only in how it is spread across products.

memory_trick.explanation: Traditional is a fixed thali bill: everyone at the table pays equally. ABC is the menu bill: you pay only for the dishes you ordered.

steps: Collect overhead in each cost pool
Pick a cost driver per pool
exam_tip: In a comparison question, name the base for each method and state the effect on low-volume complex products.

doubt.question: Does ABC reduce total cost?
doubt.answer: No. ABC only gives more accurate product costs. Cost falls only if management acts on the information, for example by dropping activities that add no value.

mistakes.wrong: ABC reduces the total overhead of the firm
mistakes.right: ABC only re-distributes the same total overhead among products more accurately.

mistakes.wrong: Labour hours are the cost driver in ABC for every pool
mistakes.right: Each activity has its own driver, such as number of set-ups, orders or inspections.

mistakes.wrong: Traditional costing over-costs low-volume complex products
mistakes.right: It tends to under-cost them and over-cost high-volume simple products.

check_notes: Checker 1: Definition 1 note ('one rate, volume only') contradicts the definition itself ('collected by department') and table row 3 ('One or few'). Traditional costing can use one plant-wide rate or separate departmental rates. Correct version: 'one or few rates, volume bases only'.

Checker 1: Memory trick explanation: 'everyone at the table pays equally' could suggest that traditional costing splits overhead equally between products. It actually charges overhead in proportion to volume (labour or machine hours), whatever activities each product really uses. Suggested wording: 'Traditional is a thali bill shared by head count: each person pays the same rate whatever they ate, so the big eaters of activities are subsidised. ABC is the menu bill: you pay for the dishes you ordered.'
